questions.question: Q1. A bilayer uses a 1 MPa hydrogel (active) and a 2 GPa PLA (passive), giving SC = 2000. Compared with SC = 100, what happens to the deformation?

answers.a: Deformation spreads evenly, reducing fold accuracy.
answers.b: At SC = 2000 almost all curvature concentrates in the soft hinge (clean fold); at SC = 100 the passive segment also bends, degrading localisation.

explanations.a: Incorrect - high SC concentrates, not spreads, the deformation.
explanations.b: Correct - a high stiffness contrast localises bending in the hinge; a low SC lets the passive layer share the deformation.
explanations.c: Incorrect - SC strongly controls where bending occurs.
explanations.d: Incorrect - high SC still allows the soft hinge to fold.

questions.question: Q2. To achieve the same target fold angle with a thinner active hinge, the required hinge length L_hinge:

answers.a: Must increase, since thinner hinges are stiffer.
answers.b: Can be shorter, because a thinner hinge is more compliant (lower I).

explanations.a: Incorrect - thinner hinges are more compliant, not stiffer.
explanations.b: Correct - since I = b h^3/12, reducing h lowers I and a shorter hinge reaches the same angle.
explanations.c: Incorrect - the dependence on h is strong (h cubed).
explanations.d: Incorrect - length is a positive quantity.

questions.question: Q3. A 4-link gripper with 3 full joints gives F = 3(4-1) - 2*3 = 3. How can the designer reach the target mobility F = 2?

answers.b: Add one half-joint, which removes one degree of freedom: F = 9 - 6 - 1 = 2.

explanations.a: Incorrect - removing a link changes F by 3 and overshoots.
explanations.b: Correct - each half joint removes 1 DOF, taking F from 3 to 2.
explanations.d: Incorrect - adding a constraint readily achieves F = 2.

questions.question: Q4. Why is the Grubler-Kutzbach criterion only approximate for compliant 4D-printed flexure hinges?

answers.a: Because it ignores the colour of the links.
answers.b: Because it assumes rigid bodies with point joints, whereas a flexure distributes deformation over a region (a continuum model is needed for thick flexures).
answers.c: Because it only works for metals.

explanations.b: Correct - compliant hinges are distributed, so the rigid-body joint idealisation breaks down for thick flexures.
explanations.c: Incorrect - the criterion is material-independent in principle.
explanations.d: Incorrect - counting joints is exactly what it does.

questions.question: Q5. In inverse kinematics, the 'positioning error' reported after folding represents:

answers.b: The distance between the achieved end-effector tip and the target point.

explanations.a: Incorrect - it is a geometric distance, not a mass.
explanations.b: Correct - it is the residual gap between the folded tip and the desired target after solving for angles.
explanations.c: Incorrect - that is a fatigue quantity.
explanations.d: Incorrect - that is a stiffness ratio.

questions.question: Q6. The rigid-origami Miura predictions deviate from reality when:

answers.b: Panel thickness exceeds roughly 5% of the panel length, so finite-thickness (Tachi-Miura) corrections are needed.

explanations.a: Incorrect - thin sheets match rigid-origami well.
explanations.b: Correct - finite panel thickness breaks the zero-thickness crease assumption beyond ~5% thickness/length.
explanations.c: Incorrect - an unfolded sheet trivially matches.

questions.question: Q7. How is the auxetic (negative Poisson's ratio) behaviour of the Miura fold verified?

answers.a: By heating the sheet until it melts.
answers.b: By observing simultaneous expansion in both lateral directions during uniaxial stretching.

explanations.a: Incorrect - melting is unrelated to Poisson's ratio.
explanations.b: Correct - an auxetic sheet expands transversely when stretched, the hallmark of a negative Poisson's ratio.
explanations.c: Incorrect - resistance does not measure Poisson's ratio.

questions.question: Q8. Basquin's Law was developed for metals. What correction is applied when using it for polymer hinges?

answers.a: None; it is exact for polymers.
answers.b: Because polymer fatigue carries about a factor-of-3 uncertainty, a safety factor of 5-10 is applied to the predicted life N.
answers.c: The exponent b is set to zero.

explanations.a: Incorrect - polymer fatigue is rate- and temperature-sensitive, so it is not exact.
explanations.b: Correct - a safety factor of 5-10 accounts for the larger scatter in polymer fatigue data.
explanations.c: Incorrect - b is a material constant, not zero.
explanations.d: Incorrect - stress is the key driver of fatigue.

questions.question: Q9. Reducing a hinge from h = 0.5 mm to h = 0.3 mm increases its fatigue life by orders of magnitude. Why is the effect so dramatic?

answers.a: Because life depends linearly on thickness.
answers.b: Because N varies as sigma^(-1/b) with 1/b = 10, so a modest stress reduction multiplies the life enormously.

explanations.a: Incorrect - the dependence is a steep power law, not linear.
explanations.b: Correct - with b = 0.1 the exponent 1/b = 10 makes fatigue life extremely sensitive to stress.

questions.question: Q10. A self-folding gripper is computed to have mobility F = 0. What does this mean for actuation?

answers.a: It will fold easily with any stimulus.
answers.b: It is over-constrained and rigid - it will not transform regardless of how strong the stimulus is.
answers.c: It has too many degrees of freedom.
answers.d: It will fold to exactly the target shape.

explanations.b: Correct - an over-constrained (F = 0) mechanism is locked and cannot move under any stimulus.
explanations.c: Incorrect - too many DOF corresponds to F greater than the target.
explanations.d: Incorrect - a locked structure cannot reach a folded target.
